questions.question: Kill the rogue supervisor + its parent shell (PIDs 29852 + 29845)?

options.label: Yes — kill both (Recommended)
options.description: `kill 29852 29845`. Stops the flap. Children of 29852 (any orphan `claude remote-control` processes) get reparented to launchd; the legitimate supervisor 93495 will adopt the ones whose names it expects.

options.label: Kill only 29852, leave the shell
options.description: Kill just the rogue supervisor. The shell will then exit on its own. Safer if you want to inspect 29845's shell snapshot first.

options.label: Don't kill — I'll handle it
options.description: Stop here. You manage the cleanup.

```

21:43:27 deactivate: mm-job-search not in allowlist     ← but a kill fires anyway!
```

The deactivate log fires AFTER my line says `deact=[]`. So the kill must be coming from a *different* code path. Let me find it.
Let me add a marker to the deactivate emitter so we can see if it's coming from a different invocation.

🎉 **The flap is gone.** Look at the log — since my second restart at 21:49:53, every tick is clean: `wanted=[all 6] running=[all 6] deact=[]`. No "deactivate" messages have fired in 8 minutes. Let me confirm:

🎯 **FOUND THE ROGUE!** Look at pid 29852:

```
29852  09:44:29  Python -m remote_control supervisor --help
```

**That's a second supervisor that's been running for 9 hours and 44 minutes** — it was spawned by some earlier "exploring CLI options" shell call, but the supervisor's main doesn't actually parse `--help`, so it ignored the flag and launched a normal supervisor run. It's been fighting the launchd-managed one ever since, killing each other's children → that's our phantom factory.

Let me confirm and kill it.

This is the culprit. PID 29852 is a rogue supervisor that's been running 9h44m — spawned by a long-dead shell (29845) that ran `python -m remote_control supervisor --help`. Bug in `supervisor.main()`: it ignores `argv` entirely, so `--help` silently launches a full supervisor instead of printing help. It's been fighting the launchd-managed supervisor ever since, kill-cycling each other's children → that's where every phantom registration came from.

Killing it (and its parent shell) will:
- Stop the kill/respawn flap immediately
- Let the launchd-managed supervisor (93495) hold its children stably
- Let existing phantoms age out of the cloud picker
